tasks.short: Find what is contaminating a brownfield site and record the source.

steps.what: Read historic land use and earlier contamination reports.

loop.input: Historic land-use files and earlier laboratory reports
loop.output: Rows for contaminant, medium, location and year
loop.check: The manager compares each contaminant with the report line
loop.stop: One pass; a contaminant with no location stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports mix maps and prose, so a fixed column map misses names

steps.what: Walk the site and sample soil, water and structures.
Analyse samples and return a laboratory certificate.
Judge which contamination source the evidence supports.
File the source finding on the site record.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store extracts a contamination clue list from historic reports. The manager walks the site, and the laboratory returns a certificate. A source finding is filed only where the certificate and the walk agree.
tasks.previous_blocker: Historic reports were paper maps and notes, so each site was reread from the start.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored report can fill contaminant, medium, location and year. The walk cannot be skipped.
tasks.still_hard: Telling an old spill from a release that is still coming from next door.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees staining, odours and fill that no report names.

ambition.what: A suspected source is named before the walk when the old report supports one, and kept or dropped on site the same day.

tasks.altitude: Walks stay on the week. Less time goes to retyping old reports. The manager can refuse a source the certificate does not support.

reach.task: Review the ground investigation before a foundation design
reach.learn: Which sources must be settled before a structure is placed on the fill

evidence.claim: A GRC platform keeps compliance, audit and incident records.
Naming a contamination source needs the sample and the walk, not only the old file.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Boundary: from historic files and a walk to a filed source finding. The remediation design is a later task.
Structured fields are contaminant, medium, location, year and suspected source. Earlier reports and the laboratory produce them. Fallback: the manager types any contaminant the extract leaves blank.
Configure the site record in the {OPS_SYSTEM} before custom code. Laboratory time is not the manager's time.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers new contaminant names on the clue list.
National environmental rules set which concentrations matter. This task does not set a legal limit.
unknowns: Whether historic reports are searchable files or paper in a cabinet.
Whether the laboratory already returns a structured certificate.
research_questions: What share of source findings change after the walk?
How often is the source a neighbour's activity rather than the site's own past?

incremental.description: Add contaminant names when the laboratory uses a new test

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: reports are maps and notes, so the clue list fails and the walk is unchanged. High: reports are readable and only the reading shrinks. Sampling and the source judgement stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run the day's cleanup on site so the permit conditions hold.

steps.what: List today's permitted cleanup tasks and hold points.
Brief the crew on site before cleanup work starts.
Carry out the cleanup tasks named in the briefing.
Judge the day's cleanup against permit compliance conditions.
Notify the regulator only when a condition is breached.
File the daily compliance log on the site record.

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} list shows the cleanup tasks the permit allows today. The manager briefs the crew from that list. A breach notice leaves only for a compliance judgement the manager has signed; a clean day is logged and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's tasks lived in a marked-up plan and in mail, so a missed hold point showed up after the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Permit tasks and hold points can drive a daily list. Directing the crew on the ground cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing, on the ground, that the crew is about to cross a hold point the list did not phrase well.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears what the crew can actually do before the weather turns.

ambition.what: Each morning the manager decides which permitted tasks may start, before the crew is briefed.

tasks.altitude: Briefings stay. Less time goes to rebuilding the day's list. The manager can refuse a task that is not on the checked list.

reach.task: Decide which permit breaches must be notified the same day
reach.learn: The compliance manager's rule for a breach versus a note in the log

evidence.claim: A GRC platform keeps compliance, audit and incident records and monitors regulatory items.
A protocol library can hold the procedure and route an incident to the person in charge.
Directing a crew on a live cleanup stays with a person on the site.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. The contractor's hours are not the manager's saving. Boundary: from the approved plan to a daily log, and a breach notice only when the manager has judged a breach.
Structured fields are task name, hold point, permit condition, owner and status. The approved plan produces them. Fallback: the manager types a task the list leaves off.
Configure the daily list on {WORKFLOW} before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers new hold points when the permit is varied.
National environmental rules decide what counts as a breach. This design does not invent that rule.
unknowns: Whether the permit conditions are already a structured list or only a scanned permit.
Who is allowed to send a breach notice, the manager or only counsel.
research_questions: How often does a day's work include a task that was not on the permit list?
What share of days end with a real breach rather than a clean log?

incremental.description: Update hold points when a permit variation is issued
Contractor still does the physical cleanup

approvals.approved_version: daily work list checked that morning
breach notice for the signed compliance judgement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the plan is a marked drawing, so the list is rebuilt by hand and the briefing is unchanged. High: tasks are already coded and only the list and the log shrink. The briefing and the compliance judgement stay. Contractor hours are not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find funding the project can claim and submit the application.

steps.what: Read funding rules, deadlines and costs the call allows.

loop.output: Rows for eligible cost, deadline, match required and excluded cost
loop.check: The manager checks each row against the call
loop.stop: One pass; a rule with no deadline stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Calls mix tables and prose, so a fixed form does not catch every exclusion

steps.what: Assemble project costs and facts the funding form asks for.
Decide which funding scheme this project can claim.
Draft the funding application from the checked fact sheet.

loop.input: The funding choice and the application fact sheet
loop.output: Draft application with each cost tied to a fact-sheet line
loop.check: The manager deletes any cost that is not on the fact sheet
loop.stop: One draft; a sentence with no fact-sheet line is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative is prose, but every figure must trace to a line

steps.what: Sign and submit the funding application to the funder.
Funder checks the submitted application against the call.

tasks.design: The grant call is read into eligibility rows, and project costs are assembled on the fact sheet in the {ERP}. The manager chooses the scheme and edits the draft. The application is submitted only after the manager signs that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Calls and cost sheets lived in separate files, so each application was retyped against a deadline.
tasks.enabler_now: Named costs and deadlines can fill a fact sheet. The claim of what the project will deliver cannot be copied from a prior bid.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which cost is honestly eligible when the call's exclusion is vague.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which part of the project a funder will not believe.

ambition.what: A small site without a bid writer can submit one complete funding application from its own cost file.

tasks.altitude: Application weeks still include a decision on what to claim. Retyping eligible costs shrinks. The manager can refuse to submit a draft that names a cost the fact sheet does not hold.

reach.task: Set which regeneration benefits the organisation will claim in bids
reach.learn: Which benefits may be promised, and which must stay out of the application

evidence.claim: A compliance review that was partly drafted by a model cited sources that were not real, and the fee was repaid.
A form with named cost lines can be filled from a fact sheet; the project claim itself cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. The funder's review is not the manager's saving. Boundary: from a grant call to a signed submission. Drawing the remediation design is out of scope.

Structured fields are eligible cost, deadline, match, excluded cost and site fact. The call and the cost file produce them. Fallback: the manager types a rule the extract leaves blank, and deletes any draft sentence with no line.
Use the funder portal's own form before a custom pack. Test that configuration before new code.
Upkeep of 6 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new call's eligibility rows.
No national funding statute is named in the digest. Follow the call's own rules.
unknowns: Whether cost estimates already exist as structured lines or only as a narrative.
Who may sign the submission, the manager or a director.
research_questions: What share of calls use a stable form rather than a free-text prospectus?
How often is an application sent back because a cost was not eligible?

incremental.description: Refresh eligibility rows when a new call is published

approvals.approved_version: draft application the manager edited and signed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the call is a prospectus and the costs are a narrative, so the fact sheet is retyped and the claim is written by hand. High: costs are already lines and only the draft shrinks. Choosing the scheme and signing stay. Funder time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the redevelopment so cleanup, safety and reuse stay inside the permit.

steps.what: Extract safety and compliance constraints from the site file.

loop.input: The site source record and the permit
loop.output: Constraint rows: medium, limit, area and standard
loop.check: The manager checks each limit against the permit clause
loop.stop: One pass; a limit with no area stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Permits state limits in clauses, not as a single table

steps.what: Set the redevelopment order for cleanup, safety and reuse.
Draft the redevelopment plan from the accepted sequence.

loop.input: The work sequence and the constraint list
loop.output: Plan sections that cite a constraint row
loop.check: The manager removes any section that cites no constraint
loop.stop: One draft; a section with no row is cut
loop.why_not_simpler: The plan is prose, but each control must point at a constraint

steps.what: Walk the redevelopment plan on site and accept a version.
Issue the accepted redevelopment plan to the build team.

tasks.design: Constraints are extracted from the permit into a list on {DOCS}. The manager sets the sequence and edits a plan that cites those rows. The plan is issued only after the site walk accepts that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Constraints were buried in the permit, so the sequence was argued from memory on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Named limits can be listed. Choosing the sequence for this ground still takes the manager.
tasks.still_hard: Ordering demolition and cleanup so a control is in place before the next trade starts.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which area of the site will not take the planned reuse.

ambition.what: The sequence is fixed against the constraint list before the site walk, not rewritten during it.

tasks.altitude: Walks stay. The manager can refuse to issue a plan section that cites no constraint.

reach.task: Sequence the build around contamination controls
reach.learn: Which controls must finish before a trade is allowed on that area

evidence.claim: A versioned policy library maps obligations to rules and flags gaps in regulatory documents.
Choosing a safe sequence for a contaminated site stays a person's judgement.
A drafted text can cite material that does not exist unless each line is tied to a source.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Boundary: from the permit and the source record to an issued plan. Daily crew direction is a separate task.
Structured fields are medium, limit, area and standard. The permit produces them. Fallback: the manager types a clause the extract leaves blank.
Use the {DOCS} template for the plan before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers new constraint types when standards change.
Applicable standards are the ones named on this permit. National rules vary and are not invented here.
unknowns: Whether the construction manager already holds a copy of the permit.
How often the reuse goal changes after the walk.
research_questions: What share of constraints are numeric limits rather than narrative conditions?
Who may accept the plan on site, the manager alone or also the landowner?

incremental.description: Revise constraint types when the permit standard changes

approvals.approved_version: draft plan version walked on site
accepted plan version from that walk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the permit is narrative, so the constraint list is typed by hand and the walk reopens the sequence. High: limits are already numeric and the draft cites them. The sequence and the walk stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still site walks, crew briefings and hearings. Constraint lists, permit fields and cost lines are ready before the visit. The manager can stop a method, a filing or a price that is not on a checked version.
reach: Construction managers: sequence demolition so contamination is not spread
Compliance managers: say which breaches are notified the same day
Regulatory affairs managers: keep the permit condition list current
skills_to_grow: Checking an extracted constraint against the source line
Reading a laboratory certificate without treating a blank as zero
Holding a filing or a price that is not the checked version
role.ambitious_version: Each site carries a versioned constraint list, each filing uses fields the manager has checked, and each on-site commitment stays inside a limit already signed.

job.title: Brownfield Redevelopment Specialists and Site Managers
